macros.name: barrier
macros.doc: You can use the \barrier command to draw a barrier in your circuit, represented as a vertical dashed line.

macros.name: cctrl
macros.doc: The commands \cctrl and \cctrlo are identical to the \ctrl and \ctrlo commands, respectively, except they use classical wires instead of quantum ones to do the controlling.

macros.name: cctrlo
macros.doc: The commands \cctrl and \cctrlo are identical to the \ctrl and \ctrlo commands, respectively, except they use classical wires instead of quantum ones to do the controlling.

macros.name: cds
macros.doc: To indicate a generalized circuit with n iterations of something, you could use the \cds command.

macros.name: control
macros.doc: The commands \control and \controlo are isolated controls; they don’t automatically connect to anything.

macros.name: controlo
macros.doc: The commands \control and \controlo are isolated controls; they don’t automatically connect to anything.

macros.name: cw
macros.doc: The classical wire commands work exactly like the quantum wire commands, but they draw double instead of single lines.

macros.name: cwx
macros.doc: The classical wire commands work exactly like the quantum wire commands, but they draw double instead of single lines.

macros.name: dstick
macros.doc: \lstick, \rstick, \ustick, and \dstick produce labels that project out to the left, right, top, and bottom respectively.

macros.name: gate
macros.doc: The \gate command draws the argument of the function inside a framed box and extends a wire back to the previous column.

macros.name: gategroup
macros.doc: \gategroup{#1}{#2}{#3}{#4}{#5}{#6} highlights the entries between rows #1 and #3 and columns #2 and #4 by adding a box or a bracket.

macros.name: ghost
macros.doc: \ghost behaves like an invisible gate that allows the quantum wires on either side of your multigate to connect correctly.

macros.name: multigate
macros.doc: \multigate{#1}{#2} is a two argument gate that takes the depth of the gate for the first argument and the label of the gate for the second argument.

macros.name: push
macros.doc: To force an object to take up space, you should use the \push command.

macros.name: Qcircuit
macros.doc: The command \Qcircuit is simply a disguised \xymatrix command with a default parameter set.

macros.name: qswap
macros.doc: Q-circuit implements a gate command called \qswap that is equivalent to the text {\times} \qw.

macros.name: qw
macros.doc: The command \qw draws a wire between two columns of a QCD.

macros.name: qwa
macros.doc: To indicate the end of a circuit simply use the \qwa command as the last wire.

macros.name: qwx
macros.doc: The command \qwx[#1] takes an optional input, #1, and connects from the current position to a position #1 entries below the current position.

macros.name: rstick
macros.doc: \lstick, \rstick, \ustick, and \dstick produce labels that project out to the left, right, top, and bottom respectively.

macros.name: ustick
macros.doc: \lstick, \rstick, \ustick, and \dstick produce labels that project out to the left, right, top, and bottom respectively.
